classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied symmetric circle to determine which coordinates change sign under reflections or a half-turn, and combine those signs for tangent.

content.prompt: Use the diagram below to express each of the following in terms of $\sin\theta$, $\cos\theta$ or $\tan\theta$. All angles are in degrees.

spec.description: Four symmetrically reflected circumference points with dashed opposite-point diameters and vertical chords. The acute first-quadrant angle is labelled θ; its drawn size is illustrative and no numerical angle is supplied. Ordinary marks are black and the circle is unshaded.
spec.mathematics: Reflection in the y-axis changes the x-coordinate sign; reflection in the x-axis changes the y-coordinate sign; a half-turn changes both signs.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source axes, points, guides and θ label are visible; no answer expressions are added.

answer.worked: Reflection in the $y$-axis preserves the $y$-coordinate. Therefore $\sin(180^{\circ}-\theta)=\sin\theta$.
Reflection in the $y$-axis reverses the $x$-coordinate. Therefore $\cos(180^{\circ}-\theta)=-\cos\theta$.

Reflection in the $y$-axis preserves $y$ and reverses $x$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan(180^{\circ}-\theta)&=\frac{\sin\theta}{-\cos\theta}\\\tan(180^{\circ}-\theta)&=-\tan\theta\end{align*}$$
A half-turn reverses both coordinates. Sine is the $y$-coordinate, so $\sin(180^{\circ}+\theta)=-\sin\theta$.
A half-turn reverses both coordinates. Cosine is the $x$-coordinate, so $\cos(180^{\circ}+\theta)=-\cos\theta$.
Reflection in the $x$-axis reverses the $y$-coordinate. Therefore $\sin(360^{\circ}-\theta)=-\sin\theta$.
Reflection in the $x$-axis preserves the $x$-coordinate. Therefore $\cos(360^{\circ}-\theta)=\cos\theta$.

Reflection in the $x$-axis reverses $y$ and preserves $x$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan(360^{\circ}-\theta)&=\frac{-\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\\\tan(360^{\circ}-\theta)&=-\tan\theta\end{align*}$$
The point for $-\theta$ is the reflection of the point for $\theta$ in the $x$-axis. Its $y$-coordinate is reversed, so $\sin(-\theta)=-\sin\theta$.
The point for $-\theta$ is the reflection of the point for $\theta$ in the $x$-axis. Its $x$-coordinate is unchanged, so $\cos(-\theta)=\cos\theta$.

Reflection in the $x$-axis reverses $y$ and preserves $x$.
$$\begin{align*}\tan(-\theta)&=\frac{-\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\\\tan(-\theta)&=-\tan\theta\end{align*}$$
